contextFacts.note: Collections totaling $180,000 from three enterprise accounts expected in August are running behind: Enterprise Account A owes $80,000, Enterprise Account B owes $60,000, and Enterprise Account C owes $40,000. These are fictional account labels. Collections are now expected in September but are not confirmed. These amounts are excluded from August's $500,000 of actual receipts. They explain the $180,000 shortfall against planned receipts, not another cash outflow or an additional deduction from the actual cash bridge.
Planned August customer collections were $680,000. Actual receipts were $500,000. The three late enterprise accounts explain the entire $180,000 collections variance.

Planned August closing cash was $1,100,000: opening cash of $1,200,000 plus planned collections of $680,000 less planned payments of $780,000. Actual payments matched the plan. Actual closing cash of $920,000 is $180,000 below plan. Without the collection delays, the month-over-month cash decline would have been $100,000 rather than $280,000.
Cash is down mainly because collections from a few enterprise customers are running behind. Three accounts explain most of the variance.
The equipment payment in cash-equipment was a one-time purchase. It is already included in the cash bridge.
